audit_findings.title: Gross-conversion share count does not match the equity-level earnings claim
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately 7.045m excess shares versus the filed Q3 diluted weighted average of 22.500m; the 29.545m denominator is 31.3% higher, and using 22.500m would raise base value from $8.06 to approximately $10.58 per share
audit_findings.evidence: Because the principal amount of the 2026 Notes and the 2030 Notes will be settled in cash with any excess conversion value settled in cash or shares of common stock, the 2026 Notes and the 2030 Notes have been excluded from the computation of diluted consolidated net income per share because the average market price of the Company’s common stock during the reporting period did not exceed the conversion prices of $ 156.34 and $ 72.23 , respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated denominator mismatch. All scenario values of $6.03-$8.90 per share are below the notes' $72.23 and $152.98 conversion prices and the $214.18 warrant strike, so gross underlying shares should not be included at those values. The error materially depresses per-share value, although correcting it alone would not close the gap to the $54.69 market price.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the scenario-specific denominator using current common shares, treasury-stock dilution for employee awards, and net-share settlement for each note and warrant after applying the partial unwind and capped-call terms.

audit_findings.title: Separate sale-leaseback amortization may be missing from the noncash add-backs
audit_findings.magnitude: potential $12.735m annual OE understatement, equal to 84.3% of the $15.1m anchor; actual adjustment remains unconfirmed
audit_findings.evidence: In 2020, the Company completed a sale and leaseback transaction involving 64 Cracker Barrel stores.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing separately reports $12.735m of sale-leaseback asset amortization outside depreciation and amortization. If the worksheet omitted it, the anchor is materially understated. The filing demonstrates the charge's size but does not establish whether the valuation already added it back.
audit_findings.action: Trace the FY2025 OE worksheet to the cash-flow reconciliation and rerun all scenarios if the $12.735m was not added back exactly once, retaining ordinary rent and lease cash costs.

audit_findings.title: The valuation perimeter may already be obsolete
audit_findings.evidence: The Company also owns Maple Street Biscuit Company (“MSBC”), a breakfast and lunch fast casual concept.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved perimeter possibility, not a demonstrated error. The May 1, 2026 filing still consolidates 52 MSBC locations, but the valuation date follows the July 20, 2026 trigger. The supplied record neither confirms closing nor separately reports MSBC earnings, proceeds, taxes, or retained obligations, so it cannot establish the size or direction of the effect.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the closing 8-K or next filed financial statements and rerun using post-closing MSBC earnings removal, net sale proceeds, taxes, transaction costs, retained leases or indemnities, and updated cash and debt.

audit_findings.title: A refinancing gain may be embedded in recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: potential $3.186m pretax OE overstatement, equal to 21.1% of the $15.1m anchor; after-tax correction unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, contemporaneously with the issuance of $345,000 aggregate principle amount of 1.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2030 (the “2030 Notes”), we used approximately $145,900 of the net proceeds from the 2030 Notes for the repurchase of $150,000 aggregate principal amount of $300,000 aggregate principal amount of 0.625% Convertible Senior Notes (the “2026 Notes”) in separate and privately negotiated transactions and recorded a gain on extinguishment of debt of $3,186.
audit_findings.explanation: The $3.186m extinguishment gain is demonstrably nonrecurring and included in FY2025 GAAP net income. Whether the OE worksheet removed it is unresolved. If retained, its size relative to the anchor makes the resulting capitalization materially overstated.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2025 OE bridge, remove the $3.186m gain and its attributable tax effect if present, retain recurring interest and debt-issuance-cost amortization, and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize a GAAP tax benefit rather than sustainable cash taxes
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 recorded an $8.653m tax benefit versus $10.328m of cash taxes, an $18.981m gap equal to 125.7% of the $15.1m anchor; sustainable adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s provision for income taxes (income tax benefit) includes employer tax credits for FICA taxes paid on employee tip income and other employer tax credits which are accounted for using the flow-through method.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate a tax amount large enough to dominate anchor OE, but they do not demonstrate the proper normalized tax charge. Recurring FICA credits may support part of the benefit, while deferred-tax timing, audit items, carrybacks, and finite carryforwards may not recur. Capitalizing the full GAAP benefit without reconciliation could materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 OE taxes to pretax operating earnings, current and deferred taxes, recurring FICA credits, other credits, audit settlements, carrybacks, and carryforward expirations; then rerun with a sustainable tax schedule that changes appropriately with forecast pretax income.
